items.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021
items.q: There was a girl that used to come and take lessons... her name was [sounds like] Mitsuyo.

ctx.x: And you know but he believes me, and there have been a few people over the years that have believed what I was telling them. There was a girl that used to come and take lessons, she came the whole summer. She played the clarinet. And I gave her this idea, that, and then I told her I said, “Now I want you to come up with a four note motif.” I said, “Don’t even think about it just come up with A, anything A through G, and label it natural, sharp or whatever, and then we’ll put it together going up or down, to get…

And boy she — when she would come for her lesson I’d have to practice a day in advance because she’d be fiddling through this — I’d have to get ready for it. But she’s the only one that I had that was that ambitious.
